# Read-Back

A Western blot is being performed on a single 10-lane gel that will be run, wet-transferred to a PVDF membrane, and probed overnight with primary antibody in a cold room. The work involves protein sample preparation (thawing, normalizing, denaturing, and spinning), running the gel in an electrophoresis tank for 75 minutes, preparing and executing a wet transfer to membrane for 60 minutes, then a series of blocking, washing, and antibody probing steps on an orbital rocker and in a cold room, finishing with substrate mixing, application, imaging and quantification. The bench has exactly one gel tank, one wet transfer tank, one orbital rocker (the bottleneck for blocking and washing), one heat block, one microcentrifuge, one cold room, and one chemiluminescence imager; the transfer tank and rocker are explicitly non-shareable, meaning the blot moves through them sequentially with no parallel operations. One operator is working. The protocol has several time-critical staging requirements: transfer buffer must chill in the cold room an hour before the transfer step begins; the PVDF membrane must be wetted and equilibrated one hour into the gel run; fibre pads and filter paper must soak in cold buffer before the transfer; and the secondary antibody probe is followed 50 minutes later by substrate mixing. No finishing deadline was stated; the protocol should complete as soon as the sequential work allows.
